Diane's 70th birthday · The finalists

Four ships, one big birthday

We narrowed it to Holland America's Eurodam, Princess's Royal Princess and Crown Princess, and the Norwegian Encore. All four sail into Glacier Bay National Park. Here they are side by side: ship size, amenities, every port, the excursions worth booking, and what it all costs for the four of us in two balcony cabins.

Meet the finalists

The four ships at a glance

Each ship keeps its own color all the way down the page, so you can follow it through the charts and tables.

Sizing them up

Big ship or small ship?

Eurodam carries about half as many guests as the Norwegian Encore. Bigger ships have more to do, while smaller ones have shorter lines, quieter decks and an easier walk from the cabin to dinner.

How to read "space per guest": it's the ship's gross tonnage divided by the number of guests, a standard way to measure how roomy a ship feels. Above 40 feels spacious. "Guests per crew member" is about service, and lower is better.

The money

What it costs the four of us

Two balcony cabins with two people each, using cruise-line fares sampled in fall 2026. The crew tip figures are the lines' standard daily rates, which are added automatically.

Not included: taxes and port fees (usually a few hundred dollars per person), flights, hotels, drinks and excursions. Crown Princess ends in Whittier, near Anchorage, so plan on a one-way flight home from Anchorage instead of a round trip to Vancouver. Each line sells a bundle of drinks, Wi-Fi and dining extras (see Amenities) that can be worth it for a celebration.

The verdict

There's no wrong answer, only the right fit

For a relaxed, scenic 70th with great food, Eurodam is the most graceful choice. For the most Alaska per day, Crown Princess wins, especially with Denali added. Royal Princess covers the classic highlights for the least money. If the group wants lots to do and a big-ship buzz, it's Norwegian Encore.

Itineraries and balcony fares from cruise-line schedules and pricing as sampled by CruiseTimetables, November 1, 2026. Ship specs from Wikipedia, Travel Weekly and cruise-line materials. Amenity details reflect the most recent refits we could confirm (Eurodam 2023, Crown Princess 2018, Norwegian Encore 2024), and venues and shows can change before 2027. Excursion prices are typical 2026 ranges, partly from Cruisebound's Alaska excursion guide. Please confirm everything with the cruise line or a travel agent before booking.
